objective: Add a local fail-closed bearer-header request gate for registered Cloud IaC OpenTofu module-registry and artifact routes while keeping health/liveness public and preserving no-production-auth/no-Cedar nonclaims.

best_practice_sources.what_it_establishes: OpenTofu CLI credentials may be configured per host or via host-specific environment variables and are used as bearer authorization tokens for service requests.
OpenTofu discovers native services at /.well-known/terraform.json and may include configured credentials in discovery and service endpoint requests.
The module registry protocol exposes service discovery, versions, and download endpoints; download responses can return a module source location.
Bearer credentials grant access to any holder and therefore must not be disclosed in storage, logs, or transport.

implemented_claims: CloudIacAppConfig parses OYA_CLOUD_IAC_MODULE_REGISTRY_BEARER into a redacted SECRET-class optional bearer value.
run_cloud_iac_app fails closed unless a valid local module-registry bearer is configured.
CloudIacAppRequestAuthPolicy validates bearer fixtures without exposing them through Debug output.
The request-auth middleware returns 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} plus WWW-Authenticate: Bearer for missing or wrong bearer headers on registered module-registry and artifact routes.
Health and liveness probes remain public.
Manifest, catalog, tasks, and evidence record the local-request-bearer-gate-no-production-auth-no-cedar nonclaim.
explicit_non_claims: no tenant identity, RBAC, ABAC, or IAM integration
no token issuance, exchange, refresh, revocation, rotation, or credential helper implementation
no TLS termination or deployed Cloud IaC endpoint
no object-store archive serving or CDN integration
no registry publish API, database adapter, or persistent registry store
no signed module releases, Sigstore/cosign execution, SLSA, or VSA attestation verification
no provider runtime, provider API calls, provider credentials, or cloud provisioning
no live Argo CD rollout, Kubernetes rollout, or Jenkins pipeline execution

no FD-001 microservice dogfood tenant workload hosting or production tenant evidence

false_green_findings_closed: Previously static in-process authorization metadata made registry route tests green while real HTTP requests had no credential requirement; the new middleware gates registered registry/artifact routes.
Previously artifact bytes could be served to an unauthenticated request after digest verification; the new auth gate runs before artifact serving for registered artifact paths.
Bearer-bearing config and policy Debug output are redacted so a local secret fixture is not printed through ordinary debug formatting.
known_gaps: This is local bearer-header checking only and intentionally does not implement production auth, Cedar, tenant identity, token lifecycle, TLS, or secret management.
Middleware executes after router match in the current Hyper adapter dispatch path; claims are limited to registered module-registry and artifact routes, not unknown-path prefix authorization.
The local artifact route still uses local filesystem archive bytes and is not object-store, CDN, or production streaming storage.
Full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required and aggregate gate run-all are not claimed by this slice.

findings: Kept the slice small: a single local middleware seam, a config env var, and tests; no production auth stack was smuggled in.
Moves the substrate toward private-registry behavior by requiring request credentials before module metadata or archive bytes are returned.
Tests cover missing bearer, wrong bearer, matching bearer, and public probes. Error responses do not reveal the expected bearer.
The app exposes a single explicit env var for local bearer configuration and preserves no-auth builders for lower-level unit seams.
Request-auth behavior is tested at app dispatch level and all prior app tests still pass. Scoped HTTP/Cloud IaC matrix remained green.

alternatives_named: Implement full production authentication/Cedar runtime now
Add a local bearer-header middleware gate
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A local bearer gate closes the immediate unauthenticated-request false green while avoiding premature production auth/Cedar claims.
rejected_reasons: Static metadata alone does not protect HTTP request surfaces.
Full production auth requires tenant identity, policy, token lifecycle, TLS, and secret-management surfaces outside this local foundation slice.

findings: Bearer values are not echoed in responses and Debug output is redacted. Missing and wrong bearers both return the same 401 response to avoid simple token-oracle distinctions.
The middleware performs one in-memory header string comparison per registered protected request. No SLO or production throughput claim is made.
This improves least-access posture for local private-registry evidence but is not a compliance certification or production access-control audit.
OpenTofu-compatible response bodies for authorized requests remain unchanged; unauthorized requests receive standard Bearer challenge metadata.
run_cloud_iac_app fails closed when no local bearer is configured, making the required local credential explicit before binding a listener.
ChangeSet is tied to Oya VCS claim, app source/tests, manifest/catalog/tasks, multispectrum evidence, and audit-chain rows.
Used Oya VCS claim; avoided raw git/gh; read root hub and operating contract; kept /plan complementary-only; did not claim production/hyperscaler completion.
No new dependencies were added. The auth gate uses existing std/http middleware seams in the app layer.

review_findings: No critical/high issues found in self-review for the local foundation scope. The route match ordering limitation is documented as a known gap.
